import { createClient } from "@supabase/supabase-js";

/**
 * Server-side Supabase client.
 *
 * Uses the service_role key, which bypasses Row Level Security.
 * NEVER import this into a client component or expose it to the browser.
 * It is only safe inside server components, route handlers, and server actions.
 */
export function createServerClient() {
  const url = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL;
  const serviceRoleKey = process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY;

  if (!url || !serviceRoleKey) {
    throw new Error(
      "Missing Supabase env vars. Set NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY."
    );
  }

  return createClient(url, serviceRoleKey, {
    auth: { persistSession: false },
  });
}

import { createServerClient } from "@/lib/supabase/server";
import type { Politician } from "@/lib/types";

/**
 * Search politicians by name / office / state / party.
 * Combines Postgres full-text search with a trigram fallback so partial
 * and slightly-misspelled names still match.
 */
export async function searchPoliticians(query: string): Promise<Politician[]> {
  const supabase = createServerClient();
  const q = query.trim();

  if (!q) {
    const { data, error } = await supabase
      .from("politicians")
      .select("*")
      .order("name", { ascending: true });

    if (error) throw error;
    return (data ?? []) as Politician[];
  }

  // ilike handles partial substring matches on the name;
  // this is simple and reliable for a name-search UI.
  const { data, error } = await supabase
    .from("politicians")
    .select("*")
    .or(
      `name.ilike.%${q}%,current_office.ilike.%${q}%,state.ilike.%${q}%,party.ilike.%${q}%`
    )
    .order("name", { ascending: true });

  if (error) throw error;
  return (data ?? []) as Politician[];
}

/** Fetch a single politician by slug for the detail page. */
export async function getPoliticianBySlug(
  slug: string
): Promise<Politician | null> {
  const supabase = createServerClient();
  const { data, error } = await supabase
    .from("politicians")
    .select("*")
    .eq("slug", slug)
    .maybeSingle();

  if (error) throw error;
  return (data as Politician) ?? null;
}

/** All slugs, used to pre-generate detail pages at build time. */
export async function getAllSlugs(): Promise<string[]> {
  const supabase = createServerClient();
  const { data, error } = await supabase.from("politicians").select("slug");
  if (error) throw error;
  return (data ?? []).map((row) => row.slug as string);
}

Created `lib/ingest.ts` — a dependency-free RSS ingest module for the Mapachusetts Next.js + TypeScript (strict) project. It type-checks cleanly (`npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0). No other files were modified.

What it does:
- `FEED_URLS: string[]` constant (default `https://rss.politico.com/congress.xml`), looped over so more feeds can be added later.
- Zero-dependency XML parsing via small regex helpers:
  - `extractItems(xml)` — pulls each `<item>...</item>` block (non-greedy).
  - `extractTag(block, tag)` — grabs `<title>`, `<link>`, `<description>`, `<pubDate>`; unwraps `<![CDATA[...]]>`.
  - `decodeEntities` — decodes `& < > " ' '` (ampersand decoded last).
  - `stripHtml` — removes tags from descriptions.
  - `cleanSnippet` — strips HTML, decodes entities, collapses whitespace, truncates to 500 chars; returns null when empty.
- Maps items to `NewArticle`: url=link and title required (items missing either are skipped), snippet=cleaned description or null, source=feed hostname (via `URL`), published_at=raw pubDate or null.
- `dedupeByUrl` de-duplicates the batch by url before a single `.upsert(rows, { onConflict: "url", ignoreDuplicates: false }).select("id")` into the `articles` table; throws on Supabase error.
- Exported `ingestArticles(): Promise<number>` runs across all feeds, is resilient (a failing feed is `console.warn`'d and skipped), and returns the stored/updated count.
- CLI entrypoint guarded by `process.argv[1]` matching `/ingest\.ts$/`, matching the requested snippet exactly.

Strict-mode compliant: no `any`, precise types/interfaces (`RssItem`), JSDoc on exported functions, and concise commenting matching `lib/politicians.ts` / `lib/supabase/server.ts`. Imports use the `@/...` alias.
